blueprint_concepts: Distance formula, Section formula, harmonic conjugate

concept_use.Distance formula, Section formula, harmo: The section formula gives P (internal) and its harmonic conjugate Q (external division in the same ratio), and OP . OQ = 0 fixes lambda = 1/2.
concept_use.Diametrical form of circle: The circle on PQ as diameter is written in diametric form (x - x1)(x - x2) + (y - y1)(y - y2) = 0, giving x^2 + y^2 + 4x - 8y = 0.

english: Let $A(-4,3)$ and $B(-10,0)$ be two points. For $\lambda>0$, $\lambda\neq1$, let $P_\lambda$ be the point that divides $AB$ internally in the ratio $\lambda:1$, and let $Q_\lambda$ be the harmonic conjugate of $P_\lambda$ with respect to $A$ and $B$. For exactly one value of $\lambda$, the circle with $P_\lambda Q_\lambda$ as a diameter passes through the origin $O$. This circle meets the $x$-axis at $O$ and at the point $(\beta,0)$. Then the value of $\beta$ is ______.
hindi: माना $A(-4,3)$ तथा $B(-10,0)$ दो बिन्दु हैं। $\lambda>0$, $\lambda\neq1$ के लिए, माना $P_\lambda$ वह बिन्दु है जो $AB$ को $\lambda:1$ के अनुपात में अन्तः विभाजित करता है, तथा $Q_\lambda$, $A$ और $B$ के सापेक्ष $P_\lambda$ का प्रसंवादी संयुग्मी (harmonic conjugate) है। $\lambda$ के ठीक एक मान के लिए, $P_\lambda Q_\lambda$ को व्यास मानकर खींचा गया वृत्त मूल बिन्दु $O$ से होकर जाता है। यह वृत्त $x$-अक्ष से $O$ पर तथा बिन्दु $(\beta,0)$ पर मिलता है। तब $\beta$ का मान ______ है।
solution: $P_\lambda=\dfrac{\lambda B+A}{\lambda+1}$, $Q_\lambda=\dfrac{\lambda B-A}{\lambda-1}$ (external division in the same ratio)
$O$ on the circle on $PQ$ as diameter $\iff\overrightarrow{OP}\cdot\overrightarrow{OQ}=0\iff\dfrac{\lambda^2|B|^2-|A|^2}{\lambda^2-1}=0\Rightarrow\lambda=\dfrac{OA}{OB}=\dfrac5{10}=\dfrac12$
(This is the Apollonius circle $\frac{XA}{XB}=\lambda$, which passes through $O$ when $\lambda=\frac{OA}{OB}$.)
solution_full: By the section formula, $P_\lambda=\dfrac{\lambda B+A}{\lambda+1}$. The harmonic conjugate of $P_\lambda$ divides $AB$ externally in the same ratio, so $Q_\lambda=\dfrac{\lambda B-A}{\lambda-1}$.
A point $X$ lies on the circle with diameter $PQ$ exactly when $\overrightarrow{XP}\cdot\overrightarrow{XQ}=0$. For $X=O$ this is $\overrightarrow{OP}\cdot\overrightarrow{OQ}=0$.
Geometric reading: the circle on $P_\lambda Q_\lambda$ is the locus of points $X$ with $XA:XB=\lambda$, so it passes through $O$ exactly when $\lambda=OA:OB=5:10$.
Diametric form: $(x+6)(x-2)+(y-2)(y-6)=0$, i.e. $x^2+y^2+4x-8y-12+12=0$, so $x^2+y^2+4x-8y=0$ (it passes through $O$, as required).
originality_note: New: the ratio of a harmonic pair is not given but fixed by requiring the diametric circle to pass through the origin, which by the dot product (or the Apollonius property) forces lambda = OA/OB (way 3). Closest known: 'the circle on the harmonic conjugates as diameter is the Apollonius circle'. Different because: the unknown is the ratio, found from O lying on the circle, and the circle is then written in diametric form.
stem_review: Read as a student: every point, line, curve and symbol is introduced before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently with sympy/mpmath (and a numerical brute-force check), is unique and equals the Answer Plan. Stated lambda > 0, lambda != 1 so that P and Q exist, and that exactly one lambda works (verified: lambda^2 = 1/4). Changed: No change.
key_step: OP . OQ = 0 reduces to lambda^2 |B|^2 = |A|^2, i.e. the Apollonius property of a harmonic pair.
justification: Two ideas linked (harmonic division and the diametric circle) with a numerical answer; the key reduction is clean but not a one-step formula. Above the plain Apollonius circle of 2025-P1-Q7 (L1) because the ratio must be found first.
